subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Steel: The Backbone of Modernity
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Steel: The Backbone of Modernity.

hook.text: The world produces 1.9 billion tons of steel per year. That's 240 kilograms for every person on Earth.

buildup.text: Steel is iron with 0.2 to 2% carbon. Too little carbon means it's soft. Too much makes it brittle.

discovery.text: Heat treatment changes steel's properties. Quenching makes it hard. Tempering makes it tough. Same metal, different uses.

twist.text: Stainless steel adds chromium, which forms an invisible oxide layer that blocks rust. Discovered by accident in 1913.

climax.text: Cars, bridges, buildings, ships, trains — steel is in nearly every structure on Earth.

punchline.text: Iron plus a pinch of carbon. That's steel.

quiz.question: What makes stainless steel resistant to rust?
options: A coating of zinc applied during manufacturing
Chromium forms an invisible oxide layer that blocks rust
It contains no iron, so there's nothing to corrode
